body:
Once a MAIN-world shim replaces window.localStorage with a namespacing Proxy, the extension must NOT read or write storage through window.localStorage any more — the proxy already strips the prefix on read and adds it on write.

Symptoms when you get this wrong, both SILENT:
- capture iterates window.localStorage looking for the namespace prefix, finds nothing (key(i) already returns the un-prefixed key), and saves an empty slice;
- restore writes prefix+key through the proxy, producing prefix+prefix+key, so the app never finds its own tokens.

Both bugs were invisible for days because localStorage PERSISTS PER ORIGIN: a reopened tab kept finding its old namespaced keys sitting there, so save/restore appeared to work. The test only became honest once it wiped the origin's storage between capture and restore.

Fix: the shim closes over the REAL Storage objects before wrapping and exposes dumpLocal/dumpSession/loadLocal/loadSession on its handle; the background goes through those and checks handle.id matches the session it intends.

Related trap in the same area: changing only a URL's #fragment is a SAME-DOCUMENT navigation, so the shim never re-runs. To move a tab into a different session you must bounce through about:blank first.
